label: Modern SaaS minimalism preference fit
weightProvenance: User-requested preference; weights and anchors authored for this skill, not empirically validated.

criteria.label: Quiet hierarchy
anchors: Chrome or decoration dominates the work; priorities are visually inverted.
Several unrelated elements compete with the main task.
Main task is visible, but headings, navigation or actions still compete.
Content leads; navigation recedes; action emphasis follows task importance.
Hierarchy stays precise in the reviewed content and states with very little competing chrome.

criteria.label: Restrained surfaces
anchors: Repeated ornate or nested containers overwhelm relationships.
Heavy shadows, pills or boxes dominate without structural purpose.
Mostly quiet surfaces with redundant card/border/depth treatments.
Flat content planes and purposeful boundaries; elevation identifies overlays.
Every reviewed boundary or layer clarifies ownership; restrained depth remains distinct in the reviewed theme.

criteria.label: Typography-led composition
anchors: Type treatment fights the desired restrained app character throughout.
Display-scale headings or excessive styles dominate routine work.
Mostly compact type roles with distracting size/weight/wrapping drift.
Compact readable sans-led UI, distinct roles, intentional weight and number alignment.
Optically careful type, wrapping and numeric rhythm carry hierarchy without unnecessary scale changes.

criteria.label: Useful density and rhythm
anchors: Empty expanses or crowding destroy the working rhythm.
Oversized padding/cards separate information needed together, or compression obscures groups.
Useful content fits, but grouping or whitespace remains uneven.
Efficient rows/groups, clear internal versus external spacing, breathing room at transitions.
Density is tuned to the screen idiom; comparisons stay close and long content retains clear rhythm.

criteria.label: Precise component language
anchors: Unrelated shapes, icons and control styles dominate.
Multiple inconsistent radii/strokes/variants make routine controls visually noisy.
A recognizable system has repeated alignment or variant inconsistencies.
Related control geometry, restrained radii and crisp icons; explicit labels where needed.
Optical alignment and states feel deliberately related; exceptions have a clear role.

criteria.label: Purposeful color
anchors: Decorative color or gradients dominate the working surface without hierarchy.
Saturated containers and competing accents dilute priority.
Quiet base with some ambiguous accent/state usage.
Neutral or low-chroma working surfaces; accents identify action, selection, data or status.
Color is sparse where appropriate and rich where meaningful; brand, state and data roles remain distinct.

criteria.label: Product-specific restraint
anchors: Generic spectacle or borrowed branding obscures product identity.
Template flourishes dominate and content feels interchangeable.
Coherent but generic treatment with limited connection to product content.
Restrained brand details, deliberate neutrality or domain-specific content ground the design in its product.
Purposeful identity or precisely judged neutrality feels specific to the work without unnecessary novelty.
